items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: It was a good orchestra. It was a dance orchestra, for that time. I don’t know whether it was his regular number of men.

ctx.x: So we know who won here. [laughs]
Well, at least somebody thought we did. They presented us with the cup, which I think says “King of Jazz” or something, you know, because . . . so that was until Paul Whiteman became King of Jazz.

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee compares Karl Kai Evans to Paul Whiteman ('he was like the Paul Whiteman of... Scandinavia') and discusses Whiteman's music in the context of F. Scott Fitzgerald's perception, but does not describe a personal interaction or professional relationship with Whiteman himself.

ctx.x: Yeah, and they carried me out of the station in to a waiting automobile and I was taken to my hotel with this crowd behind. And I was really never so thrilled, because I had not been there before, and Karl Kai Evans, who was the entrepeneur, and also a very fine musician, he was like the Paul Whiteman of, I guess we might say, Scandinavia, but especially of Denmark, and he had arranged these bookings for me, and it was a very, very wonderful reception. Yeah, he took me, I'll never forget it, he took me to the…
So obviously, then, they knew you.

ctx.x: And then in 1928, that was the time of the award that was made to that band.
That ... what was it -- did it say the King of Jazz or was it ...
Right. The Jazz King of America.
